answer: Umber Ledger Pricing. Each new agent identity must publish a signed coordination footprint—hashes of prior joint tasks—into a shared umber ledger, and pay a fee proportional to how many existing agents its claimed partners name in return. At dawn each day, fees recompute: an identity whose partners never reciprocate sits on a pricing ledge, its cost rising until farming a cluster costs more than the work it fakes. Attackers pay real per-identity fees plus repeated reciprocal-signature overhead across every sock puppet.
